issues.description: Bedrock client is opened on every inbound context frame instead of once at start/stop lifecycle
issues.detail: process_frame does `async with self._aws_session.client(...)` per LLMContextFrame, paying TLS handshake and credential resolution per turn. In a streaming voice pipeline this is a brutal constant-factor hit. Hoist client construction into start() and tear down in stop(); the session is already stored.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer calls json.loads with no try/except and will crash the pipeline on malformed lines
issues.detail: One non-JSON SSE line (heartbeat, comment, partial reconnect chunk) raises out of process_frame, aborting the stream and leaving _output_response_open=True with a dangling close task. The signature already returns Optional[str]; catch JSONDecodeError, log once, and return None so the loop stays total.

issues.description: Public parameter agentArn is camelCase, violating PEP 8 and the surrounding snake_case API
issues.detail: Every other kwarg is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). agentArn mirrors the AWS wire field but freezes that choice into public surface area. Rename to agent_arn and map to agentRuntimeArn at the boto3 call site. Torvalds also flags a class-name mismatch with the PR title (AWSAgentCoreProcessor vs AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor).

issues.description: SSE parsing is brittle: rigid `data: ` prefix check plus hardcoded line[6:] slice
issues.detail: SSE allows `data:` with no space, multiple data lines per event, and comment lines starting with `:`. startswith("data: ") + line[6:] silently drops or corrupts valid events. Use line.removeprefix("data:").lstrip() or a real SSE parser, and document the accepted grammar.

issues.description: Response bookend state machine complects a mutable flag, a timestamp, and a 1.0s racing close task
issues.detail: _output_response_open, _last_text_frame_time, and _close_task encode 'is a response open' across three places with no stated invariant. Concurrent context frames or a late-firing timer can produce unbalanced Start/End frames. Model a response segment as one value with one owner, or close explicitly when the async for ends rather than racing a wall-clock timer.

issues.description: Manual os.getenv credential fallbacks short-circuit aioboto3's resolution chain and break credential refresh
issues.detail: Reading AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET/SESSION_TOKEN manually freezes credentials at init time and bypasses shared config and instance metadata that aioboto3 already handles. Pass None through and let the SDK own credential identity-over-time; this matters for assumed roles that refresh.

synthesis.summary: Panel verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge. Three independent reviewers converge on the same lifecycle and robustness defects: a new Bedrock client opened per inbound frame, an unguarded json.loads in the default transformer that will abort the stream on any malformed SSE line, and a public camelCase agentArn parameter (plus a class-name mismatch with the PR title) that bakes inconsistency into the API. Two reviewers additionally flag brittle hand-rolled SSE parsing and a place-oriented response-bookend state machine using a 1.0s racing close task where the async-for ending already signals completion. The underlying mechanism is sound; the implementation needs the client hoisted to start/stop, total parsing functions, snake_case naming, and one explicit owner for response-segment start/end.
